newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel voices concern over Belgrade violence.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel voices concern over Belgrade violence.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Tuesday he was concerned about the violence in Belgrade and launched an appeal to all parties involved to refrain from confrontation.

"I appeal to all sides to work to prevent the political dispute from escalating into violence," Kinkel said in a statement. "The internal crisis in Yugoslavia can be resolved only through democratic dialogue and not through confrontation."

Kinkel said the entire world was closely following developments in Yugoslavia and issued a warning to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic that further violence would be detrimental to his efforts to build bridges back to Europe.

"The core question still to be answered is whether Belgrade will find its way back into the community of free and democratic states or whether that path would be blocked by abusing fundamental human rights," the German foreign minister said.

"The demonstrations today are cause for great concern," Kinkel said. "The confrontations between supporters of (Serbian President Slobodan) Milosevic and the opposition cannot be permitted to evolve into spiral of violence."
Riot police separated government and opposition demonstrators in central Belgrade after fierce street battles in which a man was shot in the head.

The intervention of police in riot armour stopped fighting between rival groups who fought each other with sticks and iron bars while crowds from both camps converged on the headquarters of the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition.
The violence was the first in 35 days of Zajedno protests against election fraud by Milosevic's ruling Socialist party (SPS).
The SPS brought thousands of supporters under police escort from all over Serbia to stage a show of support outside the Zajedno offices where the opposition holds its daily protests.
